transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Yeah, thanks. I guess I'm here because... well, what started out as just trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track has kind of turned into me cutting my meals way down. Lately, I'm basically just having black coffee, a protein shake, and a really small dinner. And I'm doing that even on shift days at the firehouse, when I know for a fact I've burned way more than what I'm actually taking in.
When you think about eating more or gaining weight, what feelings or thoughts come up for you?

Well, it's... honestly, it really stresses me out. If I step on the scale and it's up even a single pound—like after a big station meal, or even if I just drank a lot of water—I get this tight, panicked feeling in my chest. It just feels like I've completely blown it. I start thinking that if I gain weight, people are going to look at me and think I'm getting soft, or that I've lost control of myself. So the idea of eating more just brings up a lot of anxiety.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how that compares to your weight before you started cutting back on meals?

Honestly, I don't have the exact numbers to give you right now. I'm not entirely sure what I weighed before I started cutting back on my meals, and... well, I don't know my exact weight today either. I just know it's definitely gone down a fair bit, mostly because my turnout gear at the station is fitting a lot looser than it used to.
Can you tell me your current height and weight as best as you can estimate them right now?

I mean, honestly, I really don't have a good guess for you. Like I said, I just don't know the actual numbers. I'm... average height, I guess, but as for the weight itself, I try not to look at the scale directly if I can help it. I just know I've dropped a decent amount because of the way my gear feels. I don't want to just throw a number out there and be completely wrong.
Do you recall your weight from a recent physical or occupational health check at the firehouse, even if it's not today's exact number?

Yeah, we did have a fitness review recently. I still don't remember the exact number they wrote down, but... they did flag my weight. They said it was too low for my build. And like I mentioned, my gear and my station clothes are definitely hanging a lot looser now. But honestly, even after they flagged it as being too low, part of me still feels like I should keep trimming down a little more.
Would you be willing to step on the scale here in the office right now so we can get an accurate current weight and height reading?

I'd really rather not. I mean, if it's absolutely required for this appointment, I guess I have to, but... I don't want to see the number. It just messes with my head too much. If you have to weigh me, can I step on it backwards so I don't see it?

Since you'd rather not see the number yourself, would it be okay if I have my nurse take your height and weight in a way you won't see, or if I call the firehouse occupational health office to get the exact figures from your recent fitness review?

I mean... yeah, having the nurse do it here is fine. As long as I don't see the number, like I said. I'd really rather you didn't call occupational health at the firehouse. I just... I don't want to drag work into this any more than they already are, you know? So, yeah, I can just step on the scale backwards for the nurse.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since you started cutting back on your meals?
I'm a guy, so I don't get periods. That's not really something that applies to me.
Have you ever had episodes of eating a large amount of food and then making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively to compensate for it?

No, I don't do that. I don't really eat large amounts of food to begin with, so there's nothing to make up for. I just try to keep my intake low. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything like that. I do work out, obviously, for the job, but it's not to burn off some big meal.
How many weeks or months has it been since you started cutting back your meals to this level?

I honestly couldn't give you an exact timeline. It wasn't really a sudden thing where I just woke up one day and dropped my intake, you know? It just... kind of happened gradually over time. So I'm not really sure how many weeks or months it's been at this specific level.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like feeling unusually tired, dizzy, lightheaded, or cold since your weight has dropped?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I get tired sometimes after a long shift at the station, but that's just normal exhaustion, you know? I haven't felt dizzy or lightheaded at all. And I don't really get unusually cold, either. Physically, I feel fine.
Have you noticed any change in your sex drive or interest in sex since you started cutting back on your meals?
No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any difference. Things are pretty much the same as they've always been in that department. It hasn't been an issue.
Now that the nurse has recorded your height and weight, can I get those exact numbers so we can calculate your current BMI?

I actually don't know the exact numbers. I mean, I know my height is around six foot, but I didn't really look at the scale when the nurse weighed me. She just wrote it down on her clipboard. You'll probably have to check the chart she gave you to get the exact weight.
Even without exact numbers, can you estimate roughly how many pounds you think you've lost since your gear started fitting looser?

I couldn't give you an exact number of pounds, honestly. I just know that my gear and my regular station clothes hang a lot looser on me now. We actually had a fitness review at the firehouse recently, and they flagged my weight as being too low for my build. But... I don't know, even after they told me that, part of me still feels like I should keep trimming down just a little more.
